sections.skill: Distinguish saving from investing and explain the relationship between risk and return

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the difference between saving and investing?

choices.text: Saving and investing are two words for the same thing
Investing is guaranteed to earn more than saving every year
Saving always loses money, while investing never does
Saving keeps money safe and available; investing seeks growth but can lose value

questions.correct_answer: Saving keeps money safe and available; investing seeks growth but can lose value
questions.intro: Saving means setting money aside in safe, easy-to-reach places, such as insured bank accounts, for short-term goals and emergencies. Investing means buying assets, such as stocks, bonds, or funds, that may grow over time but can also lose value. Investments are not FDIC insured.
questions.feedback: Savings protect value and access; investments aim for growth with the risk of loss.
questions.topic: Saving versus investing: risk and return
sources: SEC Investor.gov (Save and invest): Investments are not federally insured, can lose value, and generally carry more risk and more potential return than insured savings. (https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/save-and-invest)

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: Which goal is generally BETTER suited to investing than to a savings account?

choices.text: An emergency fund that must be available next week
Retirement in 40 years
Rent due at the start of next month
A car repair expected in two months

questions.intro: Time horizon is how long until you need the money. Money needed soon should not be exposed to market drops. Long horizons give investments time to recover from downturns.
questions.feedback: Long time horizons suit investing; short-term needs suit savings.
questions.topic: Saving versus investing: risk and return
sources: SEC Investor.gov (Save and invest): Investments are not federally insured, can lose value, and generally carry more risk and more potential return than insured savings. (https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/save-and-invest)

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: Investment A has averaged 3% a year with small ups and downs. Investment B has averaged 9% a year but sometimes lost 30% in a year. What does this illustrate?

choices.text: Investment B is guaranteed to earn 9% every year
Investment A can never lose any money at all
Higher potential return usually comes with higher risk
Risk and return are completely unrelated to each other

questions.correct_answer: Higher potential return usually comes with higher risk
questions.intro: Risk is the chance that an investment's results will differ from what you expect, including losing money. In general, investments with higher expected returns have bigger ups and downs. Past averages do not guarantee future results.
questions.feedback: The higher-return investment comes with larger swings, including big losses.
questions.topic: Saving versus investing: risk and return

misconceptions.A: Treats an average as a guarantee

sources: SEC Investor.gov (Save and invest): Investments are not federally insured, can lose value, and generally carry more risk and more potential return than insured savings. (https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/save-and-invest)

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: A stock fund rose from $50 to $58 a share in a year. What was the percent return (no dividends)?
questions.intro: Percent return = (ending value − starting value) ÷ starting value × 100.
questions.topic: Saving versus investing: risk and return

misconceptions.A: Uses the dollar gain as a percent
misconceptions.D: Gives the ending value as a percent

questions.feedback: An insured savings account is saving.

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: An investment falls 20% one year, then rises 20% the next. Starting from $1,000, what is it worth after two years?
questions.intro: Percent changes multiply. A loss needs a larger percent gain to recover: after a 20% drop, a 20% gain does not get you back to the start.
questions.topic: Saving versus investing: risk and return

misconceptions.D: Applies the rise first and ignores order

sources: SEC Investor.gov (Save and invest): Investments are not federally insured, can lose value, and generally carry more risk and more potential return than insured savings. (https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/save-and-invest)

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: After an investment falls 50%, what percent gain is needed to return to the original value?
questions.intro: Recovery gain needed = loss ÷ remaining value.
questions.feedback: $100 → $50 after a 50% loss; doubling (a 100% gain) returns it to $100.
questions.topic: Saving versus investing: risk and return

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: Two investments both average 6% a year. Which is generally riskier?

choices.text: The one with returns between 4% and 8%
The one whose yearly returns swing between −25% and +35%
They are equally risky because their average returns match
The one that is newer to the market

questions.correct_answer: The one whose yearly returns swing between −25% and +35%
questions.intro: Volatility describes how much returns swing up and down. Two investments with the same average can have very different risk.
questions.feedback: Bigger swings mean more volatility, a common measure of risk.
questions.topic: Saving versus investing: risk and return

misconceptions.D: Age alone does not show volatility

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: What is "risk tolerance"?

choices.text: The highest return an investor can expect to earn
The minimum deposit needed to open an account
How much ups and downs an investor can handle
A guarantee against loss

questions.correct_answer: How much ups and downs an investor can handle
questions.intro: Risk tolerance is your ability and willingness to handle investment losses without abandoning your plan.
questions.feedback: Risk tolerance is about handling volatility without abandoning the plan.

questions.domain: Investing, Brokerage Accounts, and Investment Products
questions.prompt: An investment pays 2% while prices rise 3% a year. What happens to purchasing power?

choices.text: It rises by 2% a year
It falls by about 1% a year
It rises by 5% a year
It stays the same as last year

questions.correct_answer: It falls by about 1% a year
questions.intro: The real return is roughly the nominal return minus inflation.
questions.feedback: Real return ≈ 2% − 3% = −1%: money buys less over time.
